questions.q: We should never share our ______ with strangers online.
questions.e: A password is secret. We must never share it with strangers.

questions.q: If someone online makes you feel scared, tell your ______ or teacher.
questions.e: Always tell parents or a teacher if anything online scares you.

questions.q: Young children should use the internet only with an ______ nearby.
questions.e: An adult can help keep us safe on the internet.

questions.q: A pop-up says 'You won a prize! Click here'. We should ______ it.
questions.e: Such pop-ups can be tricks. We should close or ignore them.

questions.q: A stranger in an online game asks Arjun some questions. Answer yes or no.
p: (a) Should Arjun tell the stranger his school name?
no
(b) Should he agree to meet the stranger?
no
(c) Should he tell his parents about it?
yes
questions.e: Never share personal details or meet online strangers, and always tell parents.

questions.q: A computer works very fast. This feature is called ______.
questions.e: Speed means a computer can do a lot of work in a very short time.

questions.q: A computer gives correct results every time. This feature is called ______.
questions.e: Accuracy means a computer does not make mistakes if the instructions are correct.

questions.q: A computer can work for hours without getting tired or bored. This feature is called ______.
questions.e: Diligence means a computer works for long hours with the same care.

questions.q: A computer can do many different kinds of work, like drawing, typing and playing music. This feature is called ______.
questions.e: Versatility means a computer can do many different types of jobs.

questions.q: Riya keeps 5000 photos, 300 songs and many stories on her computer. Which feature of a computer helps her do this?
questions.e: A computer has a large storage capacity, so it can keep a huge amount of data.

questions.q: CPU stands for Central ______ Unit.
questions.e: CPU means Central Processing Unit, the brain of the computer.

questions.q: The three parts of the CPU are the ALU, the CU and the ______ Unit.
questions.e: The CPU has the Arithmetic Logic Unit, the Control Unit and the Memory Unit.

questions.q: ALU stands for Arithmetic and ______ Unit.
questions.e: The Arithmetic and Logic Unit does sums and compares numbers.

questions.q: Which part of the CPU controls and guides all the work of the computer?
questions.e: The Control Unit (CU) controls all the parts of the computer, like a traffic police officer.

questions.q: Devices used to give data or instructions to a computer are called ______ devices.
questions.e: Input devices, like the keyboard and mouse, send data into the computer.

questions.q: Devices that show or give us the result are called ______ devices.
questions.e: Output devices, like the monitor and printer, give us the result.

questions.q: A keyboard is an ______ device.
questions.e: We give instructions through the keyboard, so it is an input device.

questions.q: A printer is an ______ device.
questions.e: A printer gives the result on paper, so it is an output device.

questions.q: A ______ copies a picture from paper into the computer. It is an input device.
questions.e: A scanner reads a paper picture or page and sends it into the computer.

questions.q: A ______ is an input device used to record our voice.
questions.e: A microphone takes in sound, so it is an input device.

questions.q: Riya records a song on the computer and listens to it.
p: (a) Name one output device she can use to listen to the song.
speakers|speaker|headphones|headphone|earphones|earphone
(b) A touch screen takes our touch and also shows pictures. Is it used for input, output or both?
both|input and output
(c) Which input device with a stick is used to play racing games?
joystick|joy stick
questions.e: Speakers and headphones are output devices; a touch screen is both input and output; a joystick is an input device for games.

questions.q: We can send messages in a few seconds using ______.
questions.e: Email (electronic mail) sends messages through the internet in seconds.

questions.q: Online ______ lets us buy things from home using a computer.
questions.e: In online shopping we choose and order things on the internet.

questions.q: Scientists use computers to predict the ______ for the coming days.
questions.e: Weather forecasts are made using computers and satellite pictures.

questions.q: Computers at ISRO help to launch and control ______.
questions.e: ISRO uses computers to launch rockets and control satellites in space.

questions.q: The ______ key moves the cursor forward by a few spaces at once.
questions.e: Pressing Tab moves the cursor a fixed number of spaces ahead.

questions.q: Keys F1 to F12 are called ______ keys.
questions.e: F1 to F12 are function keys; each does a special job, like F1 for Help.

questions.q: The ______ key is used to cancel or stop a task.
questions.e: The Escape (Esc) key cancels the current task.

questions.q: The keys on the right side of the keyboard that look like a calculator are called the ______ keypad.
questions.e: The numeric keypad helps us type numbers quickly.

questions.q: The Home key takes the cursor to the ______ of the line.
questions.e: Home takes the cursor to the start of the line; End takes it to the end.

questions.q: Arjun typed 'i love Indiaa' and wants to correct it.
p: (a) Which key does he hold down to type a capital 'I'?
Shift
(b) Which key takes the cursor straight to the end of the line?
End
(c) Which key deletes the letter on the right side of the cursor?
Delete|Del
questions.e: Shift with a letter types a capital, End jumps to the end of the line, and Delete removes the letter to the right of the cursor.

questions.q: Moving the pointer over an item without clicking is called ______.
questions.e: When we hover over an item, a small tip often appears.

questions.q: A right click shows a list of choices called a ______ menu.
questions.e: Right-clicking opens a shortcut (context) menu with useful choices.

questions.q: The two kinds of mouse are wired and ______.
questions.e: A wireless mouse has no wire and works with a battery.

questions.q: An ______ mouse uses light to sense how it moves.
questions.e: An optical mouse has a small light under it instead of a ball.

questions.q: Riya wants to select many words at once. She holds the left button and ______ the mouse over the words.
questions.e: Dragging over words with the left button pressed selects all of them.

questions.q: The ______ tool picks up a colour from the picture.
questions.a: Color picker|Colour picker|picker|eyedropper|color picker tool|colour picker tool
questions.e: The Color picker copies a colour from the drawing so we can use it again.

questions.q: The ______ tool makes the picture look bigger so we can see small parts.
questions.e: The Magnifier zooms in on a part of the picture.

questions.q: The ______ group in Paint has ready-made shapes like rectangle, oval and star.
questions.e: The Shapes group lets us draw neat shapes quickly.

questions.q: To choose a part of the picture and move it, we use the ______ tool.
questions.e: The Select tool marks a part of the picture so we can move, copy or cut it.

questions.q: In Paint, Color 1 is the foreground colour and Color 2 is the ______ colour.
questions.e: Color 1 is used for drawing (foreground) and Color 2 for the background.

questions.q: Meera is making a Diwali card in Paint.
p: (a) Which tool will she use to write 'Happy Diwali'?
Text|A|Text tool
(b) Which tool will fill the diya with orange colour?
Fill with Color|Fill with Colour|Fill|bucket|paint bucket|Fill tool
(c) Which tool will remove an extra line?
Eraser|rubber
questions.e: Text writes words, Fill with Color colours a closed area, and Eraser removes unwanted parts.

questions.q: The screen that appears after the computer starts is the ______.
questions.e: The desktop is the main screen with icons and the taskbar.

questions.q: Files we delete go to the ______.
questions.e: Deleted files go to the Recycle Bin, from where they can be brought back.

questions.q: The picture on the desktop background is called the ______.
questions.e: The wallpaper is the picture behind the icons on the desktop.

questions.q: When a computer hangs, we switch it off and on again using one option. This is called ______.
questions.e: Restart closes everything and starts the computer again.

questions.q: Arjun wants to switch off the computer correctly.
p: (a) Which button does he click first?
Start|Start button|Windows
(b) Which option does he finally click to turn off the computer?
Shut down|shutdown
(c) After the computer shuts down, what should he switch off on the wall?
main switch|switch|main power|power supply|plug
questions.e: Click Start, then Power, then Shut down, and finally switch off the main switch.

questions.q: We should use a ______ to keep the computer safe from sudden power cuts and voltage changes.
questions.e: A UPS gives power for some time during a cut, and protects the computer.

questions.q: We should keep the computer room free from ______ and moisture.
questions.e: Dust and moisture can damage the parts of a computer.

questions.q: A program that protects a computer from viruses is called an ______.
questions.e: Antivirus software finds and removes viruses from the computer.

questions.q: A secret word used to open our account is called a ______.
questions.e: A password keeps our account safe; we must keep it secret.

questions.q: We should not open emails or links sent by ______.
questions.e: Messages from strangers may have viruses or tricks.

questions.q: Being mean to or bullying someone online is called ______.
questions.e: Cyberbullying is bullying using phones or the internet. We must report it to an adult.

questions.q: A harmful program that can damage files on a computer is called a ______.
questions.e: A computer virus spreads to other files and can damage them.

questions.q: Riya gets a message: 'Send your home address to win a free cycle!' Answer yes or no.
p: (a) Should she send her home address?
no
(b) Should she tell her parents about the message?
yes
(c) Is it safe to share our password with friends?
no
questions.e: Never share personal details or passwords online, and always tell parents about such messages.

questions.q: The physical parts of a computer that we can see and touch are called ______.
questions.e: Hardware means the physical parts like the monitor, keyboard and CPU that we can touch.

questions.q: A set of programs that tells the computer what to do is called ______.
questions.e: Software is a set of instructions (programs); we cannot touch it, but it makes the hardware work.

questions.q: Which input device is used to type letters and numbers into a computer?
questions.e: The keyboard has keys for letters, numbers and symbols, so it is used for typing.

questions.q: Which output device shows text and pictures on a screen?
questions.e: The monitor (Visual Display Unit) displays the output on a screen.

questions.q: The smallest unit of computer memory is a ______.
questions.e: A bit (binary digit) is either 0 or 1 and is the smallest unit of memory.

questions.q: A small portable storage device that is plugged into a USB port is called a ______ drive.
questions.e: A pen drive (USB flash drive) is small, portable and connects through a USB port.

questions.q: Windows is an example of an ______ system.
questions.e: Windows is an operating system; it manages the computer and lets us run other programs.

questions.q: MS Word is a ______ processing software used to type letters and stories.
questions.e: MS Word is a word processor used to type, edit and format text documents.

questions.q: Which tool in MS Paint is used to fill a closed shape with colour?
questions.a: fill with color|fill with colour|fill|paint bucket|bucket
questions.e: The Fill with colour tool (paint bucket) fills a closed area with the selected colour.

questions.q: A worldwide network of computers connected to each other is called the ______.
questions.e: The Internet is a huge network that connects computers all over the world.

questions.q: A secret word used to protect your account or computer is called a ______.
questions.e: A password keeps your account safe; it should never be shared with strangers.

questions.q: The character that moves and acts on the stage in Scratch is called a ______.
questions.e: A sprite is an object or character in Scratch, like the orange cat, that follows our scripts.

questions.q: In Scratch, the background picture of the stage is called a ______.
questions.e: A backdrop is the background of the stage; a sprite's different looks are called costumes.

questions.q: Which input device is used to copy a printed photo or page into the computer?
questions.e: A scanner reads a printed page or photo and changes it into a digital image.

questions.q: MS Paint and MS Word are examples of ______ software.
questions.e: Application software helps us do a particular task, such as drawing or typing.

questions.q: Which part of the computer is known as its brain?
questions.e: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) processes all data and instructions, so it is called the brain of the computer.

questions.q: How many bits make one byte?
questions.e: 8 bits = 1 byte. A group of 4 bits is called a nibble.

questions.q: Which memory loses all its data when the computer is switched off?
questions.e: RAM is temporary (volatile) memory; its contents are lost when the power goes off.

questions.q: 1 kilobyte (KB) is equal to how many bytes?
questions.e: In computer memory, 1 KB = 1024 bytes.

questions.q: Output printed on paper is called ______ copy.
questions.e: A printout on paper is a hard copy; output seen on the screen is a soft copy.

questions.q: A container in which files are kept together on a computer is called a ______.
questions.e: Folders help us keep related files together in an organised way.

questions.q: When you delete a file in Windows, it first goes to the ______.
questions.e: Deleted files go to the Recycle Bin, from where they can be restored if needed.

questions.q: Which shortcut key makes the selected text bold in MS Word?
questions.e: Ctrl+B makes text bold, Ctrl+I makes it italic and Ctrl+U underlines it.

questions.q: Which key is pressed in MS Word to start a new paragraph?
questions.e: Pressing Enter moves the cursor to a new line and starts a new paragraph.

questions.q: In MS Paint, which tool is used to pick up a colour from the picture itself?
questions.e: The Colour picker copies a colour from any part of the picture so it can be used again.

questions.q: While drawing with the Oval tool in Paint, which key is held down to get a perfect circle?
questions.e: Holding Shift while dragging the Oval tool draws a perfect circle; with the Rectangle tool it draws a square.

questions.q: A program such as Google Chrome used to open and view websites is called a web ______.
questions.e: A web browser lets us open and view web pages; Chrome, Edge and Firefox are browsers.

questions.q: Which symbol separates the user name and the domain name in an email address such as riya@gmail.com?
questions.e: Every email address has the @ symbol between the user name and the domain name.

questions.q: Sending hurtful or threatening messages to someone online is called cyber ______.
questions.e: Cyberbullying means troubling someone using the internet; it should be reported to a trusted adult.

questions.q: In Scratch, the 'move 10 steps' block is found in which block category?
questions.e: Motion blocks (blue) move and turn a sprite, such as 'move 10 steps' and 'turn 15 degrees'.

questions.q: A sprite is at x = 0 and faces right. It runs 'move 10 steps' inside a 'repeat 5' block. What is its x-position now?
questions.e: The move block runs 5 times: 10 × 5 = 50 steps, so x becomes 50.

questions.q: The block 'when green flag clicked' starts a script. It belongs to which block category?
questions.e: Events blocks (yellow) start scripts, for example when the green flag or a key is clicked.

questions.q: Riya has a 4 GB pen drive. How many MB is that? (1 GB = 1024 MB)
A touch screen on a mobile phone works as both an input device and an ______ device.
questions.e: We give input by touching the screen, and the same screen shows the output.

questions.q: Meera typed the heading 'My Village' and wants it in the middle of the line. Which alignment should she use?
questions.e: Centre alignment places the text in the middle between the left and right margins.

questions.q: Arjun deleted a sentence by mistake. Which shortcut key will bring it back?
questions.e: Ctrl+Z is Undo; it reverses the last action. Ctrl+Y is Redo.

questions.q: Meera wants to give a new name to her folder 'Holi Photos'. Which option should she choose after right-clicking it?
questions.e: The Rename option lets us change the name of a file or folder.

questions.q: An email says 'You have won a prize! Click this link and enter your password.' A fake message like this that tries to steal your details is called ______.
questions.e: Phishing messages pretend to be genuine to steal passwords and personal details; never click such links.

questions.q: Which of these is the strongest password?
questions.e: A strong password is long and mixes capital and small letters, numbers and special symbols.

questions.q: An email that you have written but not yet sent is saved in the ______ folder.
questions.e: Unsent emails are kept in Drafts so that you can finish and send them later.

questions.q: In Paint, Meera wants her drawing to look bigger on the screen only, without changing the actual drawing. Which tool should she use?
questions.e: The Magnifier (zoom) only changes how big the picture looks on screen; Resize changes the actual picture.

questions.q: CDs and DVDs, which are read using a laser beam, are ______ storage devices.
questions.e: CDs and DVDs are optical discs because data on them is read and written with a laser.

questions.q: Arjun types a story on his computer, prints it and then listens to music.
p: (a) Which device does he use to type the story?
keyboard|key board
(b) Which device gives him the story on paper?
printer
(c) Which output device lets him hear the music?
speaker|speakers|headphones|headphone|earphones
questions.e: The keyboard is an input device, while the printer and speakers are output devices.

questions.q: Meera's computer has 8 GB RAM and a 512 GB hard disk.
p: (a) Which of the two is the primary (main) memory?
RAM|random access memory
(b) Which of the two keeps her files saved even after the computer is switched off?
hard disk|hard disc|HDD|hard drive|hard disk drive
(c) How many MB is 8 GB? (1 GB = 1024 MB)
MB
questions.e: RAM is temporary primary memory, while the hard disk is permanent secondary storage; 8 × 1024 = 8192 MB.

questions.q: A sprite with pen down runs this script: when green flag clicked, repeat 4 [move 100 steps, turn right 90 degrees].
p: (a) Which shape does the sprite draw?
square|a square
(b) How many steps does it move in all?
steps
(c) How many degrees does it turn in all?
degrees
questions.e: Four equal sides with four 90° turns make a square: 4 × 100 = 400 steps and 4 × 90 = 360 degrees.

questions.q: Riya is writing an email to her teacher at teacher@school.in and wants to send a copy to her mother too.
p: (a) In which box should she type her teacher's email address?
To
(b) In which box should she type her mother's address to send a copy?
CC|carbon copy
(c) What is the domain name in teacher@school.in?
school.in|schoolin|school in
questions.e: The main receiver goes in To, a copy goes in CC, and the part after @ is the domain name.

questions.q: Arjun is typing a paragraph on 'My India' in MS Word.
p: (a) Which shortcut key makes the selected text italic?
Ctrl+I|Ctrl I|CtrlI|Control+I|Control I
(b) Which key deletes the character to the left of the cursor?
Backspace|back space
(c) Which shortcut key saves the document?
Ctrl+S|Ctrl S|CtrlS|Control+S|Control S
questions.e: Ctrl+I gives italics and Ctrl+S saves; Backspace removes the character to the left while Delete removes the one to the right.

questions.q: Meera saved her drawing as a file named diwali.bmp.
p: (a) What is the extension of this file?
bmp|.bmp
(b) Which program did she most likely use to make it?
Paint|MS Paint|Microsoft Paint
(c) Which key on the keyboard deletes a selected file?
Delete|Del|delete key
questions.e: The part after the dot is the extension; .bmp is the default bitmap picture format of Paint.

questions.q: In Scratch, a sprite starts at x = -100. It runs 'change x by 20' inside a 'repeat 10' block. What is its final x-position?
questions.e: It changes x by 20 ten times, i.e. by 200 in all: -100 + 200 = 100.

questions.q: While playing an online game, a stranger asks Riya to meet him alone. What is the safest thing for her to do?
questions.a: Not reply and tell a parent or teacher
questions.e: Never meet or share details with online strangers; always tell a trusted adult such as a parent or teacher.

questions.q: The first screen we see after Windows starts is called the ______.
questions.e: The desktop is the main screen of Windows, with icons, the taskbar and the Start button.

questions.q: The bar at the bottom of the Windows screen that shows the Start button and open programs is called the ______.
questions.e: The taskbar shows the Start button, open programs, the clock and other icons.

questions.q: Each page of a PowerPoint presentation is called a ______.
questions.e: A presentation is made of slides that are shown one after another.

questions.q: A PowerPoint 2007 (or later) presentation is saved with the extension ______.
questions.e: PowerPoint files use .pptx, Word files use .docx and Excel files use .xlsx.

questions.q: Software that manages the computer and helps other programs to run is called ______ software.
questions.e: System software, such as an operating system, controls the computer; application software does specific tasks.

questions.q: 1 megabyte (MB) is equal to how many kilobytes (KB)?
Which memory stores the start-up instructions permanently and can only be read, not changed?
questions.e: ROM (Read Only Memory) is permanent; its contents are not lost when the computer is switched off.

questions.q: Which input device is used to record our voice into the computer?
questions.e: A microphone takes sound as input; a speaker gives sound as output.

questions.q: Which input device reads the black and white lines printed on products in shops?
questions.a: barcode reader|barcode scanner|bar code reader|bar code scanner|barcode
questions.e: A barcode reader scans the barcode lines and sends the product details to the computer.

questions.q: In MS Word, a grid made of rows and columns is called a ______.
questions.e: A table arranges information in rows and columns; each box is called a cell.

questions.q: The address of a website, such as www.ncert.nic.in, is called a ______.
questions.e: A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is the unique address of a web page.

questions.q: The emails that you receive are stored in the ______.
questions.e: The Inbox stores received mail; sent mail goes to Sent Items.

questions.q: A harmful program that can damage files and spread from one computer to another is called a computer ______.
questions.e: A computer virus is a harmful program that can delete or damage data and spread to other computers.

questions.q: In Scratch, the area where we drag and join blocks to make a program is called the ______ area.
questions.e: Blocks are joined in the Code (Scripts) area; the result is seen on the stage.

questions.q: MS Word and MS PowerPoint are examples of ______ software.
questions.e: Application software helps users do particular tasks such as typing documents or making presentations.

questions.q: Which part of the CPU does calculations and comparisons?
questions.a: ALU|arithmetic logic unit|arithmetic and logic unit
questions.e: The ALU does arithmetic and logical work, the CU controls all operations, and the memory unit stores data.

questions.q: How many gigabytes (GB) make 1 terabyte (TB)?
A hard disk is an example of ______ memory.
questions.e: Secondary memory like the hard disk stores data permanently; RAM and ROM are primary memory.

questions.q: Which output device is used to print large drawings such as maps and building plans?
questions.e: A plotter prints large, accurate drawings like maps, charts and building designs.

questions.q: A webcam used in an online class is an ______ device.
questions.e: A webcam captures pictures and video and sends them into the computer, so it is an input device.

questions.q: To select many files one by one in Windows, we hold down the ______ key and click each file.
questions.e: Holding Ctrl while clicking selects several files that are not next to each other.

questions.q: Which shortcut key copies the selected file or text?
questions.e: Ctrl+C copies, Ctrl+X cuts and Ctrl+V pastes.

questions.q: Which feature of MS Word is used to change a word into another word everywhere in the document?
questions.e: Find and Replace (Ctrl+H) finds a word and replaces it with another throughout the document.

questions.q: Text that appears at the top of every page of a Word document is called the ______.
questions.e: The header appears at the top of every page and the footer at the bottom.

questions.q: The special effects seen when one slide changes to the next are called slide ______.
questions.e: Transitions are applied between slides; animations are applied to objects on a slide.

questions.q: Which key starts the slide show from the first slide in PowerPoint?
questions.e: F5 starts the slide show from the beginning; Shift+F5 starts it from the current slide.

questions.q: A website such as Google that helps us find information on the internet is called a ______.
questions.e: A search engine searches the web for the words we type; a browser is the program used to open websites.

questions.q: Which box in an email is used to send a copy secretly, so that other receivers do not see that address?
questions.e: Addresses in BCC (Blind Carbon Copy) are hidden from the other receivers.

questions.q: Copying someone else's work from the internet and showing it as your own is called ______.
questions.e: Plagiarism is unfair; we should always give credit to the source we use.

questions.q: In Scratch, the 'repeat' and 'forever' blocks are found in which block category?
questions.e: Control blocks (orange) include repeat, forever, wait and if-then.

questions.q: A sprite runs 'turn 15 degrees' inside a 'repeat 12' block. How many degrees does it turn in all?
questions.e: 15 × 12 = 180 degrees.

questions.q: In Scratch, a variable 'score' is set to 0. Then 'change score by 3' runs inside 'repeat 5'. What is the final value of score?
questions.e: The score increases by 3 five times: 0 + 3 × 5 = 15.

questions.q: In a flowchart, which shape is used to show a decision with Yes/No answers?
questions.e: A diamond shows a decision, a rectangle shows a process, a parallelogram shows input/output and an oval shows start/stop.

questions.q: Each song is 4 MB in size. How many such songs can be stored in a 1 GB pen drive? (1 GB = 1024 MB)
Ravi's project file is 3072 KB in size. What is its size in MB?
Meera wants the words 'Republic Day' to appear in red letters. Which option on the Home tab should she use?
questions.e: Font Colour changes the colour of the letters; Highlight only colours the background behind the text.

questions.q: Arjun inserts a table with 4 rows and 5 columns. How many cells does the table have?
questions.e: Number of cells = rows × columns = 4 × 5 = 20.

questions.q: Riya wants a picture of a bird to fly into her slide during the show. Which tab should she use to add this effect to the picture?
questions.e: Effects on objects within a slide are added from the Animations tab.

questions.q: Arjun selects a file on the desktop and presses Ctrl+X. He then opens a folder. Which shortcut should he press to move the file there?
questions.e: Cut (Ctrl+X) followed by Paste (Ctrl+V) moves a file to a new place.

questions.q: In the web address https://www.ncert.nic.in, which part shows that the website belongs to India?
questions.e: .in is the country code domain for India.

questions.q: A pop-up suddenly says 'Your computer has a virus! Click here to fix it.' What is the safest action?
questions.a: Close it without clicking the link
questions.e: Such pop-ups are often tricks to spread malware; close them and use a trusted antivirus instead.

questions.q: Which device, used in ATMs and smartphones, works as both an input and an output device?
questions.e: A touch screen takes input when touched and also displays the output.

questions.q: A computer has 4 GB RAM, a 1 TB hard disk, and Meera uses a 16 GB pen drive with it.
p: (a) Which of these is primary memory?
RAM|random access memory
(b) What is the size of the pen drive in MB? (1 GB = 1024 MB)
MB
(c) Which of the three is a portable storage device?
pen drive|pendrive|USB drive|flash drive|USB flash drive
questions.e: RAM is primary memory; 16 × 1024 = 16384 MB; a pen drive can be carried from one computer to another.

questions.q: A Scratch script: when green flag clicked, set x to 0, repeat 3 [change x by 10, wait 1 seconds].
p: (a) What is the final value of x?
(b) About how many seconds does the repeat loop take?
seconds
(c) In which block category is the 'wait 1 seconds' block found?
Control
questions.e: The loop runs 3 times, adding 10 and waiting 1 second each time: x = 30 after about 3 seconds; wait is a Control block.

questions.q: Riya is making a presentation of 8 slides on 'Diwali'.
p: (a) Which view shows all slides as small pictures so that she can rearrange them?
Slide Sorter|slide sorter view|sorter
(b) Which key ends the slide show?
Esc|escape
(c) Which tab does she use to add a picture of diyas to a slide?
Insert
questions.e: Slide Sorter view helps reorder slides, Esc ends the show and pictures are added from the Insert tab.

questions.q: Arjun gets an email from an unknown sender: 'Win a free phone! Send your parents' bank details.'
p: (a) Unwanted bulk emails like this are called ______.
spam|junk|junk mail|spam mail
(b) A fake email that tries to steal personal details is called ______.
phishing
(c) Which software should be kept updated to protect the computer from harmful attachments?
antivirus|anti-virus|anti virus|antivirus software
questions.e: Such mails are spam and phishing attempts; never reply, and keep antivirus software updated.
